sources.entry: TuckBar - Hides the menu bar on the displays you choose, covering it with your live wallpaper to reduce OLED burn-in.

summary.one_liner: TuckBar is a small macOS menu bar app that hides the menu bar on displays you choose, covering it with that display's live wallpaper to reduce OLED burn-in.
summary.what_it_does: It lets you tag specific displays so their menu bar is tucked away while other monitors keep theirs. On multi-display setups, a borderless window covers the tagged display's menu-bar strip, filled with the live wallpaper captured via ScreenCaptureKit, or with solid black, or dimmed by a slider. Hovering the top edge reveals the real bar and it re-tucks when you move away. You can untuck temporarily for 5 to 60 minutes, optionally hide the Dock while a tagged display is connected, and have it tuck on connect and restore on unplug. On a single display it falls back to macOS's native menu bar auto-hide. The README describes it as v0.1.
use_cases: prevent OLED burn-in from a static menu bar
hide the menu bar on one monitor only
reduce clutter on a secondary display
temporarily show menu bar for screen recording
notable: Per-display menu bar hiding, which macOS does not offer natively
Live wallpaper cover captured with ScreenCaptureKit, not a black bar
Hover top edge to reveal the real menu bar, then re-tucks
Reconciles on next launch if force-quit mid-tuck, restoring the bar
caveats: Single-display hiding uses the system auto-hide, which applies globally on that Mac
Seamless wallpaper cover requires Screen Recording permission; without it you get the black cover
Dynamic time-of-day wallpapers may lag briefly after a change; v0.1 and ad-hoc signed, so first launch needs right-click then Open
keywords: hide menu bar on one monitor
